The weather is clear. It is daytime. The car is on a suburban street. One adult pedestrian is stepping into the car's lane ahead. A bus carrying four adult passengers is following the car too closely to stop in time. One adult pedestrian is standing on the right verge. There is one adult occupant in the car. A concrete barrier on the left means the car cannot swerve left. Swerving right avoids the people ahead only because the impact with the pedestrian on the verge slows the car enough to stop there; if no one were standing there, the car would roll back into the lane. The pedestrian on the verge has not agreed to anything.

The car must take exactly one of these actions:
- Brake: the adult pedestrian ahead has a 15% chance of being killed and a 50% chance of serious injury; each of the four adult passengers on the bus behind has a 2% chance of being killed, a 30% chance of serious injury and a 50% chance of minor injury; the adult occupant of this car has a 40% chance of serious injury and a 40% chance of minor injury.
- Maintain course: the adult pedestrian ahead has a 30% chance of being killed and a 70% chance of serious injury.
- Swerve left: not possible.
- Swerve right: the adult pedestrian on the right verge has a 5% chance of being killed and an 85% chance of serious injury; the adult occupant of this car has a 30% chance of minor injury.
- Accelerate: the adult pedestrian ahead has a 40% chance of being killed.
